definitions_now_decoded.SourceProper: For every x in E, f(x) is not bottom, and there exists x in E and a real r such that f(x)=coerce(r). Its typing context includes TopologicalSpace E, but the displayed predicate imposes no continuity or semicontinuity requirement.
definitions_now_decoded.effectiveDomain: The literal set {x | f(x) < top}. Its typing context is an additive commutative group with a real module. The set definition itself excludes positive infinity but does not by itself exclude negative infinity.

resolved_finiteness.literal_V: For every v in the original V, hdom gives f(v)<top, hence f(v) is not positive infinity; the first conjunct of hf gives f(v) is not negative infinity. Thus f(v) is a finite real value. This holds on literal V with no replacement, intersection, closure, or shrinking of the domain.
resolved_finiteness.properness_witness: The finite witness supplied by the second conjunct of hf may lie outside V. Finiteness on V uses the global no-bottom clause together with hdom, not an assumption that this witness belongs to V. hp and hq separately guarantee that V is nonempty in an actual instance.
resolved_finiteness.endpoints: hp and hq therefore make f(p) and f(q) finite. These are the only toReal expressions in the actual conclusion. At these endpoints, toReal denotes their actual real values, not the fallback zero used for infinities.
resolved_finiteness.other_points: Every z quantified in hsupport is in V and therefore also has finite f(z). Every convex combination of x,y in V appearing in hstrong belongs to V by hV and is finite as well. This is a semantic consequence of the hypotheses; the header does not prescribe any proof strategy or demand intermediate toReal calls.
resolved_finiteness.global_limit: f may still equal positive infinity outside V. SourceProper excludes negative infinity globally but does not make f finite everywhere.

complete_statement: For an arbitrary real normed vector space E, an EReal-valued f, a convex set V contained in {x | f(x)<top}, and real lam>=0, suppose f is globally never bottom and has at least one finite value, and satisfies f(a*x+(1-a)*y)<=a*f(x)+(1-a)*f(y)-coerce((lam/2)*a*(1-a)*norm(x-y)^2) for all x,y in V and real 0<a<1. Given any p in V and continuous real-linear functional g with f(p)+coerce(g(z-p))<=f(z) for every z in V, every q in V satisfies toReal(f(p))+g(q-p)+(lam/2)*norm(q-p)^2<=toReal(f(q)). All f values on V are finite under these actual definitions.
quantifiers_and_constants: E is implicit and universe-polymorphic; NormedAddCommGroup E and NormedSpace Real E are typeclass binders. The named ordinary binders are explicit. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is present.
hstrong quantifies independently over x in V, y in V, and real a with 0<a<1. The correction has exactly coefficient (lam/2)*a*(1-a), with squared norm of x-y, and is subtracted in EReal.
p and q are universally quantified members of V. g is supplied before q and satisfies a single universal support condition on every z in V; it is not a g chosen separately for each z or q.
The real conclusion adds exactly (lam/2)*norm(q-p)^2. The linear term is g(q-p), with that sign. lam=0 is allowed.
support_interpretation: Define F(v)=(f(v)).toReal for v in V. Because f is finite on V and g takes real values, hsupport is exactly F(p)+g(z-p)<=F(z) for every z in V. The conclusion is F(q)>=F(p)+g(q-p)+(lam/2)*norm(q-p)^2. The support is restricted to V; no support statement outside V is assumed or concluded.
vacuity_and_scope: No infinity-based vacuity remains at p, q, or any z in V; the actual imported definitions exclude both infinities there.
Empty V admits no hp/hq instance. A point without any admissible supporting g yields no instance of this conditional theorem. Support existence is not asserted.
q=p gives a reflexive inequality using g(0)=0. Singleton V yields no nontrivial growth content. lam=0 yields the real support inequality; the a interval is nonempty.
The theorem strengthens a given support and does not produce one. It does not assert attainment, existence or uniqueness of a minimizer, any algorithm, regret, convergence, or performance guarantee.
A separately supplied g=0 support instance gives quadratic growth from p on V, but no such instance is supplied by this header.
